newsitem.title: USA: NYS unemployment rate steadies at 6.9 pct in Feb.
newsitem.headline: NYS unemployment rate steadies at 6.9 pct in Feb.

text.p: New York State's jobless rate steadied at 6.9 percent in February, although the state added more jobs than usual--which might suggest an improving economy--the state Department of Labor said on Tuesday.

"February's gain was approximately 10,000 higher than usual, indicating that the state's labor market is on an upward swing," said Thomas Rodick, director of the Division of Research and Statistics, in prepared remarks. The new jobs were created in education, business and engineering services.

The 6.9 percent rate was level with the year ago period for all of the state. While New York City saw a very slight improvement, as its 9.8 percent rate for February, 1997, was one percentage point lower than January, the rate stayed almost a full percent above the year-ago level of 8.9 percent.

New York State's economy grew by a total of 41,900 nonfarm jobs in February, with about half of the positions - 20,800 - created by the private sector. Services added 31,900 postions, government 21,100, manufacturing 5,300, and finance, insurance and real estate 900. But wholesale and retail trade employment shed 13,000 jobs, while construction lost 3,900 and transportation and public utilities fell 400.
